channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Iran strikes and Houston (March 2, 2026)
item.description: On Monday's show: We discuss the U.S. and Israel’s military action in Iran and the implications in politics and on the oil and gas industry.

item.title: Dow asks Texas to legalize plastic pollution from its Seadrift complex
item.description: Facing multiple lawsuits, Dow requests an “unprecedented” permit amendment to authorize its discharge of polyethylene pellets into coastal waters.

item.title: Recent report shows data centers may negatively impact Texas’ water supply
item.description: Using energy forecasts used at data centers, the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC) estimated that Texas uses 8 billion gallons of water annually.

item.title: Data: Where is Houston Police Department ramping up citations of homeless people?
item.description: Criminal enforcement of sidewalk rules has outpaced referrals to services and housing.

item.title: Hello Houston (March 2, 2026)
item.description: Today: Harris County Attorney Jonathan Fombonne discusses election integrity, NPR Pentagon reporter Tom Bowman breaks down the U.S. attack on Iran, and Harris County Commissioner Lesley Briones tells us about the “Toro District.”

item.title: One out of every seven Houston area residents know of someone detained by ICE, survey finds
item.description: Fifteen percent of greater Houston residents said they personally knew someone who had been detained, or even deported, by federal immigration authorities. That percentage increases among Hispanic residents — and those near or below the poverty line.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (March 2, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Lion dance troupe brings tradition, celebration to Lunar New Year Houston
item.description: The Soaring Phoenix Dragon and Lion Dance Association performs at Lunar New Year celebrations, grand openings and other events throughout the year.

item.title: From suburban home to 40-foot sailboat: Why some Texans choose life on the water
item.description: Sanitation crews that service marinas around Clear Lake, which is located on the Texas coast, estimated that about 140 people currently live on boats full time in the area.

item.title: Houston rodeo begins its 94th season. Here’s how it’s addressing public safety
item.description: Days after a mass shooting in Austin, state leaders have increased security measures across Texas. Millions are expected to attend Houston’s annual rodeo, which does not allow firearms.
